statement: One line holds an integer n. Print yes when n is prime - exactly two divisors, 1 and itself - and no otherwise. Trial division needs to climb only to the square root of n: divisors come in pairs d and n over d, and the smaller partner of every pair sits at or below the root, so a clean sweep up there proves primality. Guard the small values first: anything below 2 is no prime, and 2 itself is the only even one.
constraints: A square-root loop is fast enough.

example.why: Checks at 2 only (since 3 squared exceeds 7) find no divisor - 7 is prime.

hint: Loop while i times i stays at most n - no floating-point square root needed.
mistake: Letting n = 1 fall through to yes; the loop body runs zero times and the guard must catch it.
